answer.text: This is the school budget’s year end. Before FY2025 it finished within about $32,000 of budget; FY2026 left $482,118, the second year in a row far above that.

paragraphs.text: **This is a budgeting story, not a savings story.** For two years running the school budget finished about half a million dollars under, after FY2023 and FY2024 each finished about $32,000 under. Most of it sat in one line budgeted far above what it paid: private tuition, $988,630 budgeted and $466,001 spent. No document says why that line was set where it was.

**Out-of-district tuition costs more every year, even where its line looks under.** Counting both funds and both kinds, it rose from $799,715 in FY2023 to $1,054,804, $1,205,949 and $1,536,266 in FY2026, $189,277 of that being FY2027 bills. The money moved between private and collaborative, and between the general fund and the circuit breaker, so each line can look wrong while the total climbs.

**FY2026’s final number was shaped in its last two days, and FY2027 starts partly paid.** The 29 June reclassification and the 30 June prepayment together moved $522,772, more than the whole surplus. FY2027 budgets out-of-district tuition at $700,142; FY2026 spent $1,346,989 on it before the prepayment.
**The school budget finished FY2026 $482,118 under budget, the second year running far above normal.** FY2023 and FY2024 each finished about $32,000 under; FY2025 left $554,945.

**One account explains it.** Private special education tuition was budgeted at $988,630 and spent $466,001, leaving $522,629, more than the whole surplus. Every other school line together came out $40,511 short. Collaborative tuition, the other kind of out-of-district placement, ran $434,108 over. Both tuition lines missed by more than $400,000, in opposite directions.

**On 30 June the district prepaid $189,277 of FY2027 tuition out of FY2026’s budget:** collaborative invoices numbered for FY2027 were charged to FY2026 and paid in July. That payment is FY2027’s cost, not FY2026’s; left to FY2027, the FY2026 surplus would read $671,395. The day before, $333,495 of collaborative tuition was moved onto the circuit breaker, against $480,204 the budget had planned, and the circuit breaker paid none of private tuition, after 40–80% of it in each of the three years before.
**Elsewhere, the pattern is mixed.** Building upkeep left $195,934 and counselors and psychologists $191,162; paraprofessionals, special-ed contracted services and transportation ran over.

**What the record does not say:** why any line came in under or over, or whether the district stands by the 29 June entry, which the Town Manager questioned in writing and which still stood on 6 October. The school budget as a whole stayed under, so there is no deficit; what was left returns to the town’s general fund.

points.text: The school budget finished FY2023 and FY2024 about $32,000 under. FY2025 left $554,945 and FY2026 $482,118: the second big year in a row.
Private tuition left $522,629, more than the whole $482,118 school surplus; every other school line together came out $40,511 short.

Collaborative tuition charged $1,070,265, including $189,277 of next year’s invoices. The circuit breaker paid $333,495 of it; the general fund paid the other $736,770, against a $302,663 budget: $434,108 over.
No transfer covered the collaborative overrun, and none moved the private leftover: the year’s bottom line absorbed both.
The district’s FY2027 workbook budgets private tuition at $536,400 and collaborative at $163,742; FY2026 paid $466,001 and $736,770.
Counted across both funds, private tuition cost $1,164,331 in FY2025 and $466,001 in FY2026; the circuit breaker paid none of it in FY2026, after 40–80% in each of the three years before.
On 30 June, $189,277 of FY2027 collaborative tuition invoices were charged to FY2026. Left to FY2027, the school surplus would read $671,395.
Private tuition left $522,629 of its budget unspent, 53%.
Building & grounds upkeep left $195,934 of its budget unspent, 28%.
Counselors & psychologists left $191,162 of its budget unspent, 18%.
Supplies, services & everything else left $71,861 of its budget unspent, 14%.
Collaborative tuition ran $434,108 past its budget, 143% over.
Paraprofessionals ran $208,082 past its budget, 15% over.
Special-ed contracted services ran $100,262 past its budget, 79% over.
Transportation ran $67,555 past its budget, 4% over.
Town (non-school) departments stood $858,462 under budget in June; their year is not closed yet.

so.text: Heavily means at least $50,000 and at least 4% of the category’s budget, either way. Each point is a measurement; none of them says why.
